what_happened: The route said RIGHT and the planned path turned right toward the far lanes, but the policy's path kept going straight and slightly left. Approaching the intersection at about 9–10 m/s, it drove off the road onto the grass median by the palm trees, about 6 m from the human's path. No actor was involved, and the camera view looked fine until the car was already off the road.

Despite a RIGHT route command, the ego went straight through the intersection and tracked along the left side of the street directly toward parked car 68. It held ~4.4 m/s without braking as the gap closed from 32.8 m to 4.3 m, and only tried to swerve right at the last moment before hitting car 68 with its front.

After handoff, the policy's planned path drifted left toward the next lane while the route went straight and then right. The ego, at about 9.5 m/s, sideswiped actor 33, which had been driving beside it in the left lane the whole time. The lead vehicle was still about 18 m ahead, so this was not a rear-end.

After handoff the policy sped up from 8.5 to 9.2 m/s on a narrow street with cars parked on both sides. Instead of following the route to the right, its planned path drifted left over the dashed line into the left parking lane, and the ego's front left corner hit the rear of parked car 31 without braking. The rear contact came later and played no part.

Going about 7 m/s toward a signalized intersection where the route turns right, the ego's plan swung left across the tram tracks instead of following the right-turn route. Just past the stop line, the ego yawed slightly left and was flagged offroad, though it was only about 0.5–0.6 m from the human's recorded path. Such a small deviation could mean the offroad flag is marginal, coming from the map edge rather than a real departure from the road.

After handoff, the ego left the recorded path. It ended up about 8.7 m to the left of where the human drove, on the wrong side of the double-yellow centre line, even though the route command was RIGHT. It kept driving straight there at about 13 m/s without braking and hit the oncoming white van (actor 86) head-on: the gap closed from 32.5 m to 3.2 m in one second, which is a closing speed of about 29 m/s.

After crossing the intersection, the ego drifted left, about 2 m off the recorded path, into the left-side parking lane. Its speed rose slightly, from 4.4 to 4.8 m/s, and it hit the front of parked car 68 while the gap closed from 9 m to 4 m with no braking. This was a lateral drift into a parked vehicle, not a lead-vehicle or turning conflict.

The command was RIGHT, but the ego went straight through the intersection at a steady ~4.5 m/s. It then drifted toward the left curb and its front hit parked car 68, never braking as the gap closed from 33 m to 4 m. Being rear-ended came only after this front contact. The camera view was clean before impact.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s, the ego kept speeding up to about 9.4 m/s on a narrow street lined with parked cars. It also drifted left of the recorded path toward the curb, and at 6.8 s its front-left hit parked car 31, about 1.6 m left of where the human drove. The camera view was clean before the impact, and the parked car was a static obstacle, so the policy's drift caused the crash.

After taking over at 4.6s on a narrow residential street lined with parked cars, the ego kept speeding up (8.6 to 9.5 m/s). Its planned path (orange) drifted left toward the left curb instead of following the route, and at 6.8s the ego's front hit car 31, parked on the left, while it was also flagged off-road.

After handoff the policy planned a path that veered left out of its lane, toward the adjacent lane, while actor 33 was driving alongside on its left. The ego drifted left at about 9.5 m/s and sideswiped actor 33 (a lateral collision) as it approached the intersection, while the recorded human trajectory stayed in the lane.

Once the policy took over (4.7s), it steered the ego left at about 9.5 m/s while the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its orange plan drifted away from the green recorded path, and at 6.4s the ego swerved into the left lane and hit actor 33, the car alongside it there. The collision is front contact at 6.4s, with lateral contact recorded in the run aggregate. The smearing in the camera image appears only at the moment of impact, and the lead vehicle stayed about 17 m ahead.

The policy took over at 4.7s while approaching a signalised intersection at about 7 m/s. By 5.7s, as the route command switched to RIGHT, the planned path (orange) was bending left across the tram tracks, away from the right-turn route. The offroad flag fired at the stop line when the ego was only 0.5 m from where the human drove, with its right edge on the lane/curb boundary.

The policy took over at 4.7 s, and 1 s later, at about 7 m/s, the ego was flagged offroad at the stop line just before the intersection. At that point it was only about 0.5 m from the recorded human path, and its box was clipping the right road boundary where the curb flares into the right turn. The policy's planned path was also heading straight or left across the intersection, even though the route command had switched to RIGHT.

The route said RIGHT and the human drove into the right-turn lanes, but the policy kept straight and then steered left towards the left-turn/U-turn lanes. It drove up onto the grass median towards a palm tree at about 9 m/s and went offroad, 6.2 m from the recorded path.

With a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left across the yellow centerline into the oncoming lane at about 12 m/s, about 9 m from where the human drove. It stayed there and hit oncoming van 86 head-on: the gap closed by roughly 28 m/s and the ego never braked.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted left at about 12 m/s onto and across the double-yellow centre line, 7.8 m off the recorded path. It sideswiped oncoming vehicle 85 in the opposing lane at 9.0 s.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drove at a steady 12 m/s about 9 m left of the recorded path, left of the yellow center line and into the oncoming lanes. It hit oncoming vehicle 86 (a van with its headlights facing the ego) head-on without braking: the gap shrank from 33.5 m to 5.2 m within 1 s, which is too fast for a car moving the same way.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path moved right toward the turn lanes, but the policy kept a path drifting left. Coming into the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego ran onto the left median with its curb, grass and a tree, about 6.3 m from the recorded trajectory. The metrics table logged no collision, so the failure is the off-road excursion.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned path went to the right lanes, but the policy drifted left across the lanes instead. It drove up onto the grassy median with trees and left the road at 8.7s, at about 9 m/s and 6.3 m from where the human drove. No collision was recorded (all collision metrics are 0); the failure is offroad only.

The route said RIGHT. During the turn, the ego went wide at about 4 m/s and ended up 7 m off the recorded path, where its front hit parked car 90 on the far side of the cross street. A rear contact from car 112, which was crossing behind, came after the at-fault front collision.
